content:
A Republican lawmaker whose “demoralizing” response to a 10-year-old boy’s essay on electric cars drew heavy backlash this spring has officially lost her seat in Congress.

Rep. Virginia Foxx (R-N.C.) conceded to her Democratic challenger, Chuck Hubbard, on Sunday after a recount ― which Foxx herself had requested ― was completed, according to The New York Times and other outlets. She lost to Hubbard by about 330 votes.

In a statement, Foxx acknowledged “a hard-fought and thorough election process” and said voters of her district had “made their voices heard.”

“While I am saddened that I did not emerge victorious in this election, I continue to have great faith in our nation, our state and the people of North Carolina,” the 83-year-old’s statement continued, per CNN.

Hubbard, 64, similarly confirmed his win in a statement on his social media platforms, noting Foxx had “graciously conceded following the results of the recount process.”

He went on to note: “Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices.”

Hubbard’s victory means Democrats have secured at least 258 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives, giving the party its largest majority in the chamber since 1992. It also follows the “blue wave” of this month’s election night, which saw Democrats gain control of both chambers of Congress in what’s been widely characterized as a rebuke of President Donald Trump’s second term.

A staunch ally of Trump and a tough critic of higher education, Foxx was first elected to Congress in 2004 and is finishing up her 11th term.

In May, the mother of 10-year-old Christian Mango shared images of a letter Foxx had sent to her son in response to a persuasive essay he’d written about the environmental benefits of electric cars.

In her reply, Foxx railed against the boy’s suggestion of tax rebates for the owners of electric cars, arguing the federal government would have to “take that money out of the pockets of hardworking people who may not have the means to buy an electric vehicle in the first place.”

“Please ask your teacher to explain propaganda to you,” she continued. “My guess is that your teachers will not give you a good educational experience and help you learn to think as they are too interested in indoctrinating you.”

Emily Mango, who is Christian Mango’s mother, condemned Foxx’s “reprehensible” words in a scathing post on Instagram.

“We have amazing teachers who are lifelines for these kids, and teachers don’t deserve the contempt and disrespect you have shown,” she wrote.

In a follow-up post, she added: “This is a totally inappropriate response to one of her youngest constituents. Clearly she is out of touch.”

North Carolina voters, however, may not have seen the last of Foxx just yet.

According to local CBS affiliate WFMY News 2, she’s already filed paperwork to run in the 2028 race, though she has yet to issue a statement about her intentions.
